frase_gancho.texto: Aromas of vanilla and Huastec folk tunes that brighten the plains of the Gulf.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: This hall celebrates the living heritage of the coastal cultures of the Gulf of Mexico, represented by the Huastec and Totonac peoples. Set among abundant rivers, vanilla plantations, and warm plains, these groups preserve a valuable artisanal and spiritual legacy. The exhibition presents delicate pieces of women’s pottery, lace clothing, and impeccable embroidery, as well as carved masks used in the traditional dances of the Diablos and the badger dancers. The immersive atmosphere helps visitors understand how huapango guitar music, improvised verse, and agricultural ceremonies to ask for rain continue to nourish daily life.
